Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you, as a teacher, would use praise in your classroom.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the behaviourist approach to motivation.

text: According to Brophy, praise is an effective way for a teacher to motivate children. It has also been
shown that praise can be ineffective.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would design and conduct your observational study of teaching style.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one teaching style that should not cause disruptive behaviour. 
Psychology and Health
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Disruptive behaviour is sometimes caused by poor teaching style. There is a teacher whose pupils
disrupt the class. You decide to observe this teacher to determine their teaching style.

parts.text:

stress.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study that has used a recording device and one study that has used a sample
test to measure stress. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about adherence to medical advice.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have found out about adherence to medical advice, discussing
the validity of measures of adherence. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would conduct an experiment to investigate the effectiveness of patient
controlled analgesia.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe medical techniques for managing or controlling pain.

text: Patient controlled analgesia is where people can control the amount and frequency of a pain-
controlling drug they give to themselves to manage acute pain. This is instead of being given a
fixed amount of the drug at a fixed time by a medical practitioner.

parts.text:
Suggest how you would investigate whether the cause of the accident was due to ‘Theory A’
or ‘Theory B’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe two accidents that could be attributed to ‘Theory A’. 
Psychology and Environment
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Reason (2000) categorises the causes of accidents into what he calls ‘Theory A’ and ‘Theory B’.
There has been an accident in a workplace and you have been sent to investigate the cause.

parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by the term ‘noise’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Using examples, describe factors that make noise annoying, such as those suggested by
Kryter.

Psychology and Abnormality
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Pigeons are said to navigate (way-find) using a substance in their brain called magnetite. Humans
may also use magnetite to way-find.

Answer this question.

Answer one question.

parts.text:
Suggest how you would investigate the relationship between biochemical and psychological
factors in impulse control disorders.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe how biochemical and psychological factors may interact to explain one impulse

text: Impulse control disorders are often said to be caused by a combination of factors.

parts.text:
Suggest how you could use an observation to investigate whether the behaviour of a person
is compulsive.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe both the psychodynamic and biochemical explanations for obsessive-compulsive
disorder. 
Psychology and Organisations
Section A
Answer this question.

text: A compulsion is a recurring action the person is forced to enact. Psychologists wonder what
causes these actions and want to find out whether they are really compulsive.

text: In 1970, Maslow extended his theory of motivation from five to eight needs.
